proposals.evidence: Tentative khaṇḍa fragment/part family. CDIAL3792 gives Kalasha khōṇḍa half, Sindhi khanu piece of bread, Punjabi khannā half, and Kumauni dwī-khan two halves. Perder p91 explicitly calls kʰana part/half and illustrates kʰani in half-past-three. These provide close semantic and structural comparanda, but Dameli n for older ṇḍ and vowel length must be independently explained; the matching Sindhi/Punjabi simplification is not itself proof of a Dameli sound law. Proposed as a difficult comparative-family link, with inheritance versus regional borrowing still open. No specifically Nuristani donor established.

The attested dū-o-kʰana two and a half contains dū two and kʰana half with coordinating -o. Record the two lexical constituents in order; -o is the coordinating clitic, not a separate lexical ancestor. This transparent structural proposal is conditional on resolving the independently proposed half base in this batch. It does not make the historical khaṇḍa analysis more certain.
proposals.save_dependency: Historical half-base proposal 1 requires review; do not save this quantity independently through an unlinked base.

approval: User: approve all; prefer Pashto where best matched, then Urdu for broadly Perso-Arabic terms. Approval includes qualified analyses, not a claim that uncertainties are resolved.
donor_policy: Prefer an attested Pashto donor where form and meaning fit best; otherwise prefer Urdu for broadly shared Perso-Arabic loans. Preserve explicit source attribution, phonological uncertainty and possible Nuristani mediation. Do not substitute a different dialect merely because its node is linkable.
